LESSON: BIBLE

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The
Topic 2.6: Bible

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Bible. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How did Moses 4 lessons b) discuss how Moses expressed obedience express obedience?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Bible means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya
3. practise Bible in clear steps
4. apply Bible in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BIBLE
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Bible helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BIBLE
Study Bible like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Bible means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Bible means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Bible means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Bible” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Bible means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Bible in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Bible in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Bible in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Bible in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Bible in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Bible in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Bible in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Bible in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Bible” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Bible in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Bible is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Bible” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Bible means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Bible in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Bible in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Bible” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Bible in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Bible to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Bible means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Bible in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Bible from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Bible: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Bible?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How did Moses 4 lessons b) discuss how Moses expressed obedience express obedience?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Bible means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Bible means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Bible from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
